items.readme:
Leonida Continued

Grand Theft Auto VI (Xbox Series) running natively on Windows, built on your PC from your own copy.

Other languages | Status | How to build | How it works | Want to help? | Credits | License | Discord | Telegram

Leonida is a static recompilation project. The Xbox Series CPU is x86-64 like a PC, so the game's code is loaded and run natively, and the console's system software is reimplemented. The console's precompiled RDNA2 GPU programs are translated to SPIR-V for Vulkan. The game's models, textures and audio are read from your package. All of this happens **on your PC, from your own copy of the game**. > [!IMPORTANT] > This repository **does not contain the game, keys or an executable**, and it does not explain how to get them. You > need your own copy, with its files already readable on disk. Nothing here decrypts or works around any protection. > Everything the build creates (the generated shaders, extracted assets, the runtime folder and your saves) comes > from your game and stays on your PC. Never share those files. > [!NOTE] > **This is a continuation of [NotRexed's Leonida project](https://github.com/ProjectLeonida/Leonida).** The original > author has left the project, and development continues here with its full commit history. Credit for the work up to > that point belongs to NotRexed and the contributors listed in the history. Discord: https://discord.gg/ETf4qj5acN Telegram: https://t.me/mandyport
## Project status **Early. Nothing is playable yet.** On `main`, the game boots from your own copy on native Windows and on Linux through Proton: it shows the launch movie, the first-run pages and the landing prompt, which respond to a pad or the keyboard pad, then runs the story load to its end and enters the world phase. A first world frame has not been verified yet on any test machine. On native Windows a scripted pad alone (`LEONIDA_INPUT_SCRIPT`, no keyboard or controller) gets through every first-run page, including the legal-terms page whose Confirm waits for both boxes, to the loading screen of the story load ([the route](docs/first_run_ui.md#through-the-first-run-pages-with-the-scripted-pad)). [First-run UI on Windows](docs/first_run_ui.md) has the build and launch steps; [the Linux/Proton report](docs/linux_proton.md) has the timings and where it stops. | What | Status | |---|---| | Booting the game | ⚠️ Through the story load into the world phase, on native Windows and Linux/Proton; no world frame verified yet ([report](docs/linux_proton.md)) | | Story mode, anything playable | ❌ No | | Finding and checking your copy (Xbox Series 1.0.2.1) | ✅ Works | | Shaders: carve, unpack native RDNA2 code, disassemble | ✅ All 26,503 | | Shaders: RDNA2 → SPIR-V translation | ✅ **26,503 / 26,503 translated**: 2,236 VS, 12,101 PS, 2,689 CS, 9,282 mesh, 195 geometry, with a per-shader metadata index for pipeline creation. The LLVM 23.1.5 Linux rerun at `c432cdc` and the LLVM 23.1.3 Windows rerun at `43d0015` both translated all 26,503 ([Linux](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/644#issuecomment-7072972586), [Windows](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/644#issuecomment-7074299915)). Translation and SPIR-V validation are separate steps; validation results are listed below. ⚠️ 23,841 are wave64: exact on 64-wide subgroups (AMD). On 32-wide subgroups (NVIDIA, Intel), compute and mesh shaders are exact with wave64 emulation (`--wave64-emulate`, on by default there); cross-half wave ops in vertex, pixel and geometry shaders are still approximate | | SPIR-V validation (`spirv-val`) | ✅ **26,503 / 26,503 passed** in the LLVM 23.1.5 Linux rerun at `c432cdc` and in the full-corpus rerun at `43d4703`, after `dcd8ecf` fixed the SPIR-V ID-bound error ([Linux rerun](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/644#issuecomment-7072972586), [full-corpus rerun](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/881#issuecomment-7075507328)). On Windows at `43d0015`, all 26,503 translated but 26,501 passed validation; the two ID-bound failures were fixed by `dcd8ecf`. The intermediate `dedd75c` run also passed 26,501. | | Shader translator checked on a real GPU | ⚠️ The hand-written GPU tests (vertex fetch, texture sampling, exports, ALU ops, partial-register ops, barycentrics, wave-uniform branches, compute LDS/barriers/buffer stores, wave64 masks) have been run on more than 30 GPU and driver combinations, with results in [#166](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/166): NVIDIA Turing, Ampere, Ada and Blackwell (Windows and Linux); AMD GCN3, RDNA1, RDNA2, RDNA3 and RDNA4 (Windows driver and RADV); Intel Gen9 (ANV); Apple M1 (MoltenVK, no geometry or mesh stages); and Mesa llvmpipe. Wave64 tests need 64-wide subgroups (AMD) or `LEONIDA_W64_EMULATE=1`. These are small test shaders: the game's own shaders are checked by `spirv-val` and by driver pipeline creation (`vk_pipeline_check`), not by their output | | Models (OBJ with real names, UVs, material references) | ✅ Exported. A ten-archive scan at decoder pin `e293917` recovered **382,781 models** with zero readback decode failures. This includes **343,327** models from `levels.rpf`. A full OBJ export of that archive is pending. See [recount and export scope](docs/models.md#full-archive-re-count-at-e293917). | | Texture dictionaries and world texture pools (DDS) | ✅ Exported. `rpf9dump` decodes BCPack BC1, BC3, BC4 and BC5 chunks in strict mode and skips BC6H, BC7 and chunks that need unconfirmed history; the assets stage then completes what it can with a clean-room decoder (`tools/bcpack.py`, which `tools/ttpf_assets.py` runs through `tools/ttpf_mips.py`) that rebuilds BC1, BC3, BC4, BC5, BC6H and BC7, and records the rest as a `BCPackLimitation` in `manifest.json` (most BC6H/BC7 chunks and the unconfirmed-history ones need a local history table, which the repo does not ship) ([notes](docs/textures.md)) | | Audio banks (AWC: Opus, XMA2) | ✅ Exported whole. Opus repackaged **losslessly** as Ogg Opus; PCM (codec 0/2) as WAV; XMA2 decoded with ffmpeg. `--wav` adds 16-bit PCM WAV ([notes](docs/audio.md)) | | Music/radio config | ? Measured. **1,589** audio-config records with exact durations and AWC stream ids; station grouping and content-id lists; no per-track start offsets ([notes](docs/audio_config.md)) | | PE loader and import shims | ⚠️ Runs a stand-in executable end to end (`gta6rt --run`: CRT startup, statics, heap, files, threads, GDK imports through the shims, exit code back). Controllers through a GameInput shim on SDL3 (any controller SDL supports, rumble, DualSense trigger effects and lightbar; built when SDL3 is installed or with `-DLEONIDA_SDL3_FETCH=ON`, [notes](docs/gameinput.md)). `--trace-d3d12` logs every D3D12 call and its outcome for the first boot. Runs the game's own executable through the story load ([report](docs/linux_proton.md)) | | Xbox D3D12 → Vulkan | ⚠️ In progress. A Vulkan-backed device behind the Xbox-ABI proxy creates queues, command lists, fences, descriptor heaps, committed, placed and reserved resources, render-target and depth views (3D targets included), texture views and samplers (2D, cube, 1D and 3D views, the depth and stencil planes of depth-stencil textures, packed formats such as B5G6R5, B4G4R4A4 and R9G9B9E5, buffer SRVs — raw, structured and typed; they go into the bindless set), root signatures, pipelines and query heaps, and draws run on Vulkan. Barriers, clears, uploads, copies (BC included), colour resolves, predication, CPU-side texture reads and writes, and occlusion, timestamp and pipeline-statistics queries run on Vulkan, checked on one GPU. The console-shaped command-list proxy, the measured `PresentX` queue slots (30/32, layout-detected) wired to the presentation core, and `AllocateUploadMemory` (list slot 148, a mapped-upload arena whose addresses translate to buffer device addresses in root descriptors and IA/SO views) cover the console-ABI surface the package measures. Still open: the console list tail and the descriptor-table record model ([plan](docs/d3d12_vulkan.md), [console ABI](docs/d3d12_xs_console_abi.md)) | | Ray tracing (BVH) | ⚠️ In progress. `BuildRaytracingAccelerationStructure` builds BLASes and TLASes on the GPU in the console's XDXR BVH4 layout (the default; `LEONIDA_RT_AS=khr` uses Vulkan's own acceleration structures instead), which the translated shaders walk themselves through `image_bvh_intersect_ray` (all four triangle node types, TRI0-TRI3, with the barycentric remap byte); the GPU builder writes TRI0 and TRI1 leaves. Updates refit instead of rebuilding, and clone, compaction and the compacted/current postbuild sizes work; checked against a CPU reference on synthetic scenes. The build descriptions are recovered from the package's `XboxBvhBuilder.dll` ([notes](docs/xdxr.md)). The game's `*_bvh4.rpf` packs are measured: offline-built, dehydrated BLASes that rehydrate through that DLL with their geometry from the drawables in `levels.rpf` (measured on 8 of the 10 sampled BLAS; [notes](docs/bvh.md)). Not done in the builder: serialization. TRI1 pairing (no memory saved yet) and BOX16 nodes for `MINIMIZE_MEMORY` BLASes (an assumed switch) are in ([notes](docs/bvh.md)). Open: whether the game rehydrates the packs or rebuilds them ([#313](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/313)) | The table above is written by hand. To measure it on your own checkout (unit and runtime tests, which rows of the translator contract were confirmed on a GPU, measured imports, your corpus counts and, with `--github`, CI and the `D3D-` items), run `python -I tools/progress_dashboard.py --out ` and open `progress.html` ([notes](docs/progress_dashboard.md)). ## Platforms Nothing is playable on any platform yet (see *Project status*). What runs where today: | Platform | Today | |---|---| | Windows | Everything: `make_game.py`, the tools, and the runtime (`gta6rt` and the D3D12 → Vulkan layer) with its tests. | | Linux | The translator, the asset tools and the Vulkan GPU test tools build and run natively (tested on RADV and NVIDIA). The runtime is Windows code: it cross-compiles with clang-cl and xwin, and its tests run under Wine or Proton (*The Windows runtime on Linux, under Wine or Proton* below). The game runs the same way, under Proton with the D3D12 layer on native Vulkan, so far through the story load ([report](docs/linux_proton.md)) (#217). `./Build.sh` starts the build; [docs/linux.md](docs/linux.md) has the packages and the steps. | | macOS (Apple Silicon) | The Python tools and the Vulkan test tools run natively, on MoltenVK (Homebrew) or KosmicKrisp. The runtime is Windows code and runs as on Linux, under Wine: CrossOver, arm64 with FEX or x86-64 under Rosetta (#1706, #1707, #1924; #3119 fixes the last loader tests there). Known gaps: no geometry stage and no `VK_EXT_mesh_shader` (those tests are skipped), 32-wide subgroups (wave64 shaders run emulated), and MoltenVK's float handling (`PerVertexKHR`, NaN compares, -0, the cost of `NoContraction`); [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md) lists each (#2947). | | AMD RDNA1 (RX 5000) | A supported target: close to the console's RDNA2, and its 64-wide subgroups run the wave64 shaders natively. RX 5700 XT results pass the GPU test suite (#146); on RADV, pixel shaders without fragment barycentrics have a known difference (*Known problems* in [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md)) (#330). | GPU results from every platform are collected in #166; how to run the tests is in [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md). ## How to build The port isn't downloaded ready-made. It's built on your PC from your own copy. **The easy way:** 1. Install the prerequisites below. 2. Download this project **with its submodule**: `git clone --recursive https://github.com/ubiquitarianism/leonida`. A "Download ZIP" from GitHub leaves out `third_party/rpf9-explorer`. The build fetches it if `git` is installed, and otherwise tells you what to do. 3. Double-click **`Build.bat`**. On Linux or macOS, run **`./Build.sh`** from a terminal instead (see [docs/linux.md](docs/linux.md) for Linux). It finds your copy of the game by itself: it looks in Downloads, Desktop, Documents (also where Windows keeps them, such as in OneDrive), Games, your home folder and the top of every drive, two folders deep. It recognises the version from a few file sizes, without reading anything large. If you have more than one copy it asks which one, and if it finds none it asks you to paste the folder. Before starting it checks that everything below is installed and that there is enough free space, and it lists anything missing in one go. The result goes to `Documents\Leonida`. A stopped build continues where it left off. Your game folder is the one that holds `MicrosoftGame.Config` and the `.rpf` archives, as plain files. **Prerequisites:** - **Your own copy** of the Xbox Series package, version 1.0.2.1. - **Windows 10/11 x64**, with about **400 GB** free for work files (an assets export alone measured about 337 GB before its audio step, in about 2 h 35 min). Disk sizes here are as Windows Explorer shows them, which are GiB: 400 GiB is about 430 GB in decimal units. They can go on another drive with `--work`. - [Python 3.12+](https://www.python.org/downloads/) (tick "Add python.exe to PATH"). - [.NET 8 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0). - [Vulkan SDK](https://vulkan.lunarg.com/), for `spirv-as` / `spirv-val`. - [LLVM 21+](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/releases) with the **AMDGPU target** for `llvm-mc`. The official Windows build has no AMDGPU target. On Windows, `scripts\build_llvm_mc.ps1` builds a native `llvm-mc.exe` with it (no WSL; needs git and the Visual Studio C++ tools below) and sets `LLVM_MC`; it takes about 20-40 minutes. A faster way, if you use [conda](https://docs.conda.io/): `conda install -c conda-forge llvm-tools` (its Windows build includes the AMDGPU target; [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md) used version 23.1.6), then set `LLVM_MC` to the full path of the `llvm-mc.exe` it installs (`where.exe llvm-mc` shows it once the environment is active; in PowerShell a bare `where` is `Where-Object`). Or install `llvm-21` in WSL and set `LLVM_MC` to the whole command, `LLVM_MC="wsl -d Ubuntu -e /usr/lib/llvm-21/bin/llvm-mc"` (see [docs/design.md](docs/design.md#disassembling-shaders)). On Linux, `llvm-mc` on PATH is enough, and so is a versioned distribution install such as Ubuntu's `llvm-21` (`llvm-mc-21`, `/usr/lib/llvm-21/bin/llvm-mc`). - Visual Studio 2022 with **Desktop development with C++** and the **Windows SDK 10.0.26100 or newer**, for the runtime stage (the runtime uses version 1.2 root signatures, which older SDKs don't declare). - [ffmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org/download.html) on PATH (optional: decodes the XMA2 streams, and required for `--wav`). **Is this PC strong enough?** [Can I Run Leonida](https://assttro.github.io/can-i-run-leonida/) is a lightweight browser-based checker that compares your PC against reference profiles. It's a rough estimate, not a benchmark. **Low disk space:** the ~400 GB figure is for the full build. To *run* the port, `--stages check,shaders,runtime` needs about 30 GB; the `assets` stage (~370 GB) is only for the asset tools, and `--wav` adds several times the Ogg Opus size (the preflight prints this choice when the assets stage is what does not fit). `--work` and `--out` can sit on another drive. The runtime maps the package in place, so a read-only package drive needs `gta6rt --overlay `; `--overlay` is a `gta6rt` option, not a `make_game.py` one. Leave the `.s` files in `work/shaders/dxbc/disasm` in place: the next run checks them against the list in `disasm.done` and disassembles the missing ones again (all of them for a folder whose `disasm.done` predates that list), then translates every shader again. A `disasm` folder that is a symlink is refused when the stage has to clear it. **Disk space and drives:** the build uses three folders, and each can be on its own drive: | Folder | Flag | What is in it | Size | Read when playing | |---|---|---|---|---| | your package | `--game` | your copy of the game; only read, never written | as copied | yes, in place (`game_path.txt`) | | work | `--work` (default `\work`) | `shaders` (carved, disassembled, translated) and `assets` (exports) | about 30 GB + about 370 GB | only `shaders\spirv` (`shader_path.txt`) | | port | `--out` (default `Documents\Leonida`) | `gta6rt.exe`, its DLL, the path files, the pipeline cache, `overlay` | small | yes | The free-space check before a build counts the `--work` drive only, because that is where the large files go. Nothing in `\assets` is read by the game, so with a small SSD you can keep what the game loads on the SSD and put the exports on a hard drive, in two runs: ```powershell # on the SSD: the package, the port and the translated shaders (about 30 GB of work files) python -I make_game.py --game "S:\Games\package" --out "S:\Games\Leonida" --work "S:\Games\Leonida\work" --stages check,shaders,runtime,pipelines # on the hard drive: the asset exports (about 370 GB), only for the asset tools python -I make_game.py --game "S:\Games\package" --out "S:\Games\Leonida" --work "H:\leonida-assets" --stages check,assets ``` The second run does not rebuild the runtime, so `shader_path.txt` keeps pointing at the SSD. Pass the same `--work` again for later runs of each stage so they resume. A single `--work "H:\leonida-work"` also works; the game then loads its translated shaders from that drive. **From a terminal**, with the same behaviour and more control: ```powershell python -I make_game.py --find # list the copies found on this PC python -I make_game.py --pick # choose the game folder in a folder dialog python -I make_game.py --check # check your copy, build nothing python -I make_game.py --check --full-check # also compare SHA-256 of every file (slow) python -I make_game.py --game "D:\path\to\your\package" --out "D:\Games\Leonida" --work "E:\leonida-work" python -I make_game.py --stages shaders,assets # only some stages python -I make_game.py --game "D:\path\to\your\package" --wav # also decode Opus to PCM WAV (large) python -I make_game.py --wave64-emulate off # auto (default), on or off; see below ``` `--wave64-emulate` decides whether wave64 compute and mesh shaders are translated to be exact on any subgroup size (see "Wave64 emulation" in [docs/design.md](docs/design.md)). NVIDIA and Intel GPUs have 32-wide subgroups and need it. The default, `auto`, asks `vulkaninfo` (part of the Vulkan SDK) and turns emulation on if any GPU lacks 64-wide subgroups or its subgroup size is unknown. It also checks whether the runtime's GPU can run compute and mesh shaders 64-wide. With `--mesh-compute`, only compute subgroup support is needed. On AMD's Windows driver, `auto` uses native wave64 on RDNA1 and RDNA2 when the runtime's GPU supports it, even if another GPU is 32-wide or `vulkaninfo` is unavailable. That driver can crash on emulated LDS code (#857). For RDNA1 cards without mesh support, the decision uses the compute stage, which can run wave64 without native mesh support. The mode is saved next to the translated shaders, and changing it translates them again. `auto` can normally reuse previously emulated shaders. The AMD Windows workaround rebuilds those shaders in native mode. Use `--wave64-emulate on` to force emulation or `--wave64-emulate off` to force native wave64. Four fallback flags are forwarded to the translator the same way, saved next to the translated shaders, and changing them translates them again: `--no-float-controls` (drop `SignedZeroInfNanPreserve`, for devices whose pipeline check skips a shader without `shaderSignedZeroInfNanPreserveFloat32`; needs PR #664's translator flag), `--bary-fallback` (read raw barycentrics from an interpolated input, for devices without `VK_KHR_fragment_shader_barycentric`), `--texel-offset-fallback` (fold `image_sample*_o` offsets into the coordinate, for devices without `VK_KHR_maintenance8`) and `--mesh-compute` (mesh shaders as compute, for devices without `VK_EXT_mesh_shader`; on by itself on Intel's Windows Vulkan driver, whose native mesh draws crash, BUILD-2202, unless `--native-mesh`). Each is documented in [docs/design.md](docs/design.md). The build records which llvm-mc command and version produced the disassembly. Changing either, or reusing a work folder that predates this record, reruns disassembly and translation while keeping the extracted shader inputs. The build records which translator sources produced the shaders. A change to those files reruns translation using the saved disassembly. Older work folders need one translation after upgrading to record this information. The build also records which decoder (the `third_party/rpf9-explorer` commit and the `tools/rpf9dump` sources) exported each archive's models and textures and each texture pool. When it changes, the assets stage removes that export and makes it again. Older work folders have no record, so their models, textures and pools are exported once more after upgrading. Stages: `check` always runs first; then `shaders`, `assets` and `runtime` run together when selected (they do not depend on each other). `pipelines` starts once the translated shaders are ready and, when this run includes runtime, that stage has finished rebuilding `vk_pipeline_check`, so it can overlap the rest of assets; it creates every translated shader on your GPU driver, reports any it has to skip, and saves a pipeline cache to `pipeline_cache.bin` in `--out`, which also holds `gta6rt.exe` after the `runtime` stage. The runtime seeds its Vulkan pipeline cache from the file beside the executable when its header matches the device and pipeline cache UUID. It falls back to an empty cache if the file is missing, incompatible, or rejected by the driver. Shader translation is the longest CPU step. It runs on `--jobs` processes (half the CPU threads by default). When shaders and assets share the machine, that budget is split between them and passed to `rpf9dump` as `--jobs`. A solo assets run still lets `rpf9dump` use every core. Progress lines include percent and a rough ETA for translation shards, asset steps, and overall stage completion. On an interactive terminal, a LEONIDA setup screen lets you set jobs and whether stages overlap, then a key-switchable per-stage log view (`1`–`4` / `Tab`) keeps parallel output demuxed; full stage logs go under `work/logs/`. Use `--no-tui` (or redirect stdout) for the plain console. `--wav` is off by default because 16-bit PCM WAV is several times larger than Ogg Opus. It decodes the repackaged Ogg Opus streams to `work\assets\audio\wav` after the audio bank step; existing WAV files are skipped when a build resumes. ### Vulkan diagnostics on Linux With CMake 3.24+, a C++20 compiler, and Vulkan development headers and loader installed: ```sh cmake -S runtime -B runtime/build/linux cmake --build runtime/build/linux --parallel ./runtime/build/linux/vk_pipeline_check /path/to/spirv ``` Pass the directory containing `index.json` and the translated SPIR-V files to `vk_pipeline_check`. `make_game.py` runs on Linux too. The `pipelines` stage uses the `vk_pipeline_check` built above (`runtime/build/linux`, or `runtime/build`), and builds it there itself before any other work if it is missing. ### Running the loader on Linux The loader is a Windows program and runs under Wine or Proton; CI runs its tests under Wine on every push to `main` that changes `runtime/`, and on demand from the Actions tab (the `wine` job of the Runtime workflow). On Linux the `runtime` stage cross-builds it into `runtime/build/windows` with clang-cl and lld-link (LLVM 19+, but not 22.1.7 or 22.1.8, see [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md#known-problems); plain names, or all five LLVM tools with one version suffix such as `clang-cl-21`) against the MSVC CRT and Windows SDK that [xwin](https://github.com/Jake-Shadle/xwin) lays out, in `XWIN_DIR` or `~/.local/share/xwin-sdk` ([docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md#the-windows-runtime-on-linux-under-wine-or-proton) has the one-time `xwin` command). Without them the stage is left out of the default stages, and asking for it lists what is missing before any work starts. A Windows build made elsewhere works too, such as the `runtime-windows` artifact of that workflow's `windows` job, unzipped: ```sh python3 -I make_game.py --runtime-build ~/Downloads/runtime-windows ``` Either way it copies `gta6rt.exe` and `gta6rt_tls_host.dll` into `--out` and writes `gta6rt.sh` next to them, which starts `gta6rt.exe` with `wine`, or with the Wine named by `WINE` (for Proton, its `files/bin/wine`). The same option skips the build on Windows. For `tools/pe_inspect.py`'s import classes on Linux, set `WINEPREFIX` to the prefix the loader runs in (or use `~/.wine`); without one, system DLLs are reported as `system (unverified)` ([docs/design.md](docs/design.md#day-one-when-the-exe-is-here)). On Linux, run `/gta6rt.sh --dry-run` to inspect the packaged title's imports, then `/gta6rt.sh --init` to check TLS callbacks and DLL initialization. Use `/gta6rt.sh --run` for startup. These commands use the package in `game_path.txt`, the port's `overlay` for writes, and Vulkan by default. When the Vulkan backend is selected with `LEONIDA_D3D12=vulkan`, the packaged runtime finds the translated shaders in `/shaders/spirv` using `shader_path.txt` beside `gta6rt.exe`. Set `LEONIDA_SHADERS` to use another directory. ### Starting the game: the launcher Double-click **`Launcher.bat`** (Linux: `python3 tools/leonida_launcher.py`) for the Leonida Launcher: a window with a PLAY button, the game and data folders, the runtime's options (DLSS, ray tracing, Smooth Motion, and so on), the mod list and a few tools. PLAY runs `scripts\play-d3d12.ps1` for you. It needs only Python and Tkinter, and is described in [docs/launcher.md](docs/launcher.md). ## How it works | Piece | What it does | Where | |---|---|---| | Version check | Every package file's name, size and SHA-256 for each supported version | `game/`, `make_game.py` | | Shader pipeline | Carves DXBC containers from `shaders.rpf` without its encrypted table of contents. Unpacks the `XBCH` → `FSSM` native RDNA2 program, disassembles it with LLVM (`gfx1013`) and translates it to SPIR-V | `tools/shader_carve.py` ([optional Rust scanner](tools/shader_carve_native/README.md)), `fssm_unpack.py`, `shader_disasm.py`, `rdna2spirv.py` | | Asset export | Finds validated resources inside RPF9 archives and the loose `.ttpf` texture pools | `tools/rpf9dump` (on rpf9-explorer's Core) | | Runtime | Maps the PE image, resolves imports to shims (GDK, XMem, `d3d12_xs`) | `runtime/` | | Research tools | PE/RTTI inspection, raw carving, texture tiling probes, GPU test harnesses | `tools/`, `runtime/test/` | | Progress dashboard | One offline page of what passes, what changed since it last passed and what blocks next, built from test results and the docs' own tables; nothing is written inside the repo | `tools/progress_dashboard.py` | Localized string tables are decoded by `tools/text_tables.py` ([docs/text.md](docs/text.md)); their language is guessed from script (kana, hangul, CJK, Cyrillic, Arabic) or Latin words, and subtitles are joined to dialogue lines across languages. The translator's runtime contract (user SGPRs, push constants, memory model, bindless images, vertex fetch, system values) and all the format notes are in [docs/design.md](docs/design.md); the format, asset, runtime and validation notes are indexed in [docs/README.md](docs/README.md). The Xbox D3D12 plan is in [docs/d3d12_vulkan.md](docs/d3d12_vulkan.md). Audio bank formats and the export tools are in [docs/audio.md](docs/audio.md); [docs/related_projects.md](docs/related_projects.md) records the prior art we may read and the licence limits on it. ## Want to help? The biggest open pieces: - **World start**: the story load finishes, but no world frame has been verified yet; [Where it stops](docs/linux_proton.md#where-it-stops) lists what stops it. - **Shader translator on hardware**: compute, mesh and geometry now translate (see the translator contract in [docs/design.md](docs/design.md)); still open is wave64 cross-half code in VS/PS/GS on 32-wide subgroups. The vertex-shader input layout is measured: all 2,236 VS are legacy (non-NGG), with `v0` = `VertexIndex` (the *Inputs and outputs* row of [docs/design.md](docs/design.md)). - **Xbox D3D12 → Vulkan**: mesh-shader draws, indirect draw state and stream output are still open; #313 tracks the remaining method surface. The Windows integration exercises the first-run UI. [Plan and status](docs/d3d12_vulkan.md) - **Model recovery**: investigate the 71 unrecovered fragment candidates in [`levels.rpf`](docs/models.md#full-archive-re-count-at-e293917). See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Never attach game files, extracted assets or generated shaders to issues or pull requests. ## Credits - [Leonida](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida) by NotRexed and contributors: the original project, which this repository continues. - [rpf9-explorer](https://github.com/breadbbbb/rpf9-explorer) by breadbbbb: the RPF9 model, texture-pool and AWC decoders used by `tools/rpf9dump` (git submodule). - [Mesa](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa) (MIT): GFX10 resource-descriptor layout (`tools/gfx10_formats.json`), and the ACO/RADV rules used as reference for 16-bit results and shader system registers. - [libHttpClient](https://github.com/microsoft/libHttpClient) (MIT) by Microsoft: the XTaskQueue/XAsync implementation in `third_party/xtaskqueue`, used by the offline `xgameruntime` shim. - [LLVM](https://llvm.org/): AMDGPU disassembler. - Logo: ["Grand Theft Auto VI" icon by SlyDevil](https://www.steamgriddb.com/icon/122618) on SteamGridDB. - [SPIRV-Tools](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/SPIRV-Tools): assembly and validation. - Aki-Developer: `aki-gta6/aki-runtime` (GPL-3.0), a sister port shared with the project. Taken from it into the Rust D3D12 runtime: the count of dropped draws by reason in the frame line, descriptor slots given back as soon as the card has run a submission, pixel colours held to the console's HDR range, the composer's clamp that keeps a NaN from coming out black, two planes composed into 10 bits under frame generation, the paired form of wave64 programs tried before the approximate ones (`LEONIDA_PAIRED_LANES=exact`), a pipeline's kept skip answer, and four small fixes it carried from fxceless/victory-fork. Each commit names the `aki-runtime` commit it is from. Grand Theft Auto and all related names are trademarks of their owners. # Introducing OpenGame OpenGame is **the first open-source Super Game Agent** — turning **DeepSeek (DSH)**, **Claude Code**, **Codex**, or any of your local coding agents into an AI Unreal Engine / Unity and full-stack game studio. Go from a single idea to **AAA-grade 3D worlds** or **monetization-ready viral mini-games** in one end-to-end pipeline. - 🚀 **Build AAA-Grade 3D Games with Your Agent.** Drive full-stack 3D gameplay, art, music, and voice straight from **DeepSeek (DSH)**, **Claude**, **Codex**, or **Gemini** — from one prompt to playable 3D action, racing, and open-world games. - 🎮 **One-Click Remix & Re-style Any Game.** Start from **25 built-in playable templates** (3D, voxel, anime, pixel & 9:16 hits) with full editable source — keep proven mechanics while swapping characters, worlds, and art styles in minutes. - 💰 **Build Games That Earn: Create → Verify → Monetize.** Automated logic checks, balance simulation, headless playtesting, covers, and gameplay trailers — ship live web links, export single-file **9:16 Playable Ads**, and connect publishing paths for **WeChat Mini Games**, **TikTok**, and **Douyin**. - 🔓 **Full-Stack Open Source (BYOA + BYOK).** Code, art, video, music, voice, SFX, and Three.js 3D are all open source — plug in your favorite [local agent](#agent-wall) and own API keys, or connect [OpenDesign Go](https://go.open-design.ai/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=opengame&utm_content=readme_en) (Black Friday lowest-ever discount, with free access to **DeepSeek V4.1 Flash**, **Seedream**, and more). ## ⚡ Quick Start ### 1. Complete the local Studio & MCP setup below so your agent can call the 12 `openmotion_game_*` tools and open Game Studio. ### 3. Run OpenGame Studio locally from source Requires **Git**, **Git LFS**, **npm**, and **Node.js 22.18+** (CI pins Node.js 26.11.1). Browse the catalog immediately after startup. Playing or remixing a template downloads its assets on first use. ## ✨ Why OpenGame ### 1. One-Click Remix & Re-style — Powered by Game-as-Code Building a polished game from a blank prompt is hard for any model. OpenGame solves this by separating **verified game engineering** from **theme, art direction, and content**: - **Every game is clean, inspectable source**: `index.html`, deterministic `logic.js`, vendored Three.js for 3D titles, plus structured design docs (`design/plan.md`, `design/style.md`, `design/assets.csv`, `design/verification.md`). - **Remix in one click**: Click **Remix** on any of the 25 templates in Game Studio (or ask your agent to remix it) to fork an owned, editable draft with full controls, tuning knobs, and automated test hooks already wired up. - **Re-style into any universe**: Swap genre dressing, characters, palette, sprites, textures, and music without breaking physics or win/loss rules — ideal for fast iteration with affordable models like **DeepSeek**, or pushing AAA-grade 3D & shader ambition with **Claude Fable 5.2**, **Opus**, **Codex**, and **Gemini**. **Try these prompts in your connected Agent:** ```text # 1. One-click Remix & Re-style (great for DeepSeek / fast models) Use openmotion-game to remix the "Lantern Hop" template into a cyberpunk rain-city cat runner. Keep the double-jump physics and endless scoring loop, replace the fox and lanterns with a neon cyber-cat and holo-batteries, generate new key art and synthwave BGM, then validate, playtest, and capture a fresh cover. ``` ```text # 2. Build a 9:16 Playable Ad ready for mobile campaigns Use openmotion-game to create a portrait 9:16 playable ad (playableAd: true) for a medieval tower-defense mobile game: instant first-frame interaction with a hand tutorial, a 25-second escalating wave battle, and an end card with an App Store / Google Play CTA. Validate, simulate, playtest at 390x844, and bundle as a single-file HTML. ``` ```text # 3. Original 3D Game from Scratch (great for Claude Fable 5.2 / Opus / Codex / Gemini) Use openmotion-game to create a 3D wuxia boss-duel game (style: "3d") set on a misty bamboo cliff at dusk. Include parry timing, dodge i-frames, stamina management, and two boss phases. Run 3-tier simulation, headless Chromium playtest, capture a 1280x720 cover, and record a gameplay trailer. ``` ### 2. Full-Stack Multimodal Game Creation (BYOK) A real game needs more than code — it needs key art, character sprites, seamless 3D textures, music loops, voice lines, and crisp sound effects. OpenGame's **Model Gateway** wires multimodal generation directly into the game project while keeping your API keys local and separate from game source.


| Game Asset Layer | Recommended Models (when configured in Model Gateway) | Zero-Key / Built-in Fallback | | --- | --- | --- | | **🖼️ Key art, portraits, sprites & textures** | `GPT Image 2.6` (edits & transparent PNGs), `Seedream 5.5` / `5.0 Flash`, `Nano Banana 2`, `FLUX`, `Codex Image` | Crisp procedural Canvas/SVG sprites & procedural textures | | **🎵 Background music (menu, stage, boss)** | `ElevenLabs Music v2` (`no vocals` loops), `Suno v4` | Procedural Web Audio synthesized soundtrack | | **🎙️ Character voice & announcer lines** | `ElevenLabs v3` (English & multilingual), `BytePlus TTS 2` (Chinese), `Kokoro` | Styled dialogue captions & subtitle UI | | **🎬 Intro cutscenes & motion clips** | `Wan 2.7`, `Seedance 2.5` (short I2V clips) | In-engine animated intro camera & title sequence | | **🔊 Impact SFX (hits, jumps, coins, UI)** | Synthesized directly in game code via the Web Audio API | Same (zero latency, zero external files) | | **🧊 3D scenes & models** | Vendored **Three.js** + bundled CC0 kits + reserved 3D gateway slot (auto-discovered when connected) | Procedural Three.js geometry, lighting & shaders | > OpenGame charges no software subscription for the local open-source stack. Use your own provider keys in **Model Settings**, connect [OpenDesign Go](https://go.open-design.ai/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=opengame&utm_content=readme_en) for unified multi-model access, or build 100% code-generated zero-API-cost games. [Model catalog](gateway/catalog.ts) · [Provider setup](docs/model-gateway.md) ### 3. Automated Game QA, Balance Simulation & Auto-Trailers Agents shouldn't just output code and hope it runs. OpenGame enforces an automated engineering verification loop before marking any game **ready**: 1. **Static & 50-Tick Logic Validation (`openmotion_game_validate`)** — Verifies `index.html`, allowed asset/CDN policies, required deterministic exports, and runs a 50-tick smoke test (`< 5 ms` per tick). 2. **3-Tier Deterministic Balance Simulation (`openmotion_game_simulate`)** — Executes bounded headless routes without a browser to verify that a skilled `reference` route reaches a real win milestone, a degraded weak route struggles, and an `idle` player loses cleanly (`< 2500` ticks). 3. **Headless Chromium Playtesting (`openmotion_game_playtest`)** — Drives real keyboard/mouse/touch controls across 1–4 clients, checking 3C responsiveness, `390×844` mobile layout integrity, media URL loads, and zero console/network errors. 4. **Game-Only Cover Capture (`openmotion_game_capture_cover`)** — Captures a clean `1280×720` PNG directly from the game canvas in isolated headless Chrome. 5. **Automated Gameplay Trailer (`openmotion_game_trailer`)** — Records three real 5-second headless gameplay clips at `1280×720`, composes an editable ~19-second title + highlights + Play Now trailer, and renders an MP4 ready for social launch. ## 🚀 End-to-End Distribution & Monetization Turn playable prototypes into real games people can play, share, and pay for. | Stage | Available Today | Roadmap (In Progress) | | --- | --- | --- | | **Play & Local Catalog** | Publish straight to your local OpenGame Studio market (`openmotion_game_publish`) with play tracking, favorites, and 1-click Remix | **Top 100 Profitable Mini-Game Templates** curated by genre & revenue mechanics for instant remixing | | **Instant Web Share** | One-click static bundle & live web share link via OpenDesign Cloud (`openmotion_assets_use action="web_publish"`), rewriting local media URLs and compressing assets automatically | Custom domain & embeddable game widget cards | | **Mobile Playable Ads** | Built-in **9:16 Playable Ad mode** (`playableAd: true`): first-frame instant play, hand tutorial, rich short-level progression, looping BGM, and App Store / Google Play end-card CTA | Direct ad-network packaging presets (AppLovin, Unity Ads, Meta, TikTok) | | **Mini-Game Platforms & Monetization** | Clean self-contained HTML5/JS project exports ready for manual platform wrapping, plus auto-recorded gameplay trailers for launch marketing | **L1–L4 Guided Platform Publishing** (packaging scripts, checklists & Skills) for **WeChat Mini Games (微信小游戏)**, **Douyin Mini Games (抖音小游戏)**, **TikTok**, **Xiaohongshu Mini-Tools**, and **itch.io / Poki / CrazyGames** | | **AI Game Playground** | Local single-player & existing room-based playtesting | **Multi-Model Live Game Arena** — pit multiple frontier LLMs against each other inside live games in real time | ## 🛠️ Setup & MCP Tools ### Connect Your Local Agent Choose your agent to connect the local OpenGame MCP server and Skills:

- **DeepSeek TUI / Harness** · Install the `openmotion-game` skill and connect the local MCP tools via Cordis configuration, or run `node integrations/dsh/install.ts` from the checkout. [DeepSeek Harness guide](docs/agent-adapters.md#deepseek-harness) - **Claude Code** · Add the stdio MCP entry below, install the `openmotion-game` skill, and run `/mcp` to verify the tools are active. - **Codex CLI** · Run `bash scripts/install-motion.command` from the checkout to register the local plugin and MCP server automatically. - **WorkBuddy** · Import the connector or paste the `mcp.json` configuration below. [WorkBuddy guide](docs/agent-adapters.md#workbuddy) #### Manual stdio MCP configuration (works in any MCP client) ```json { "mcpServers": { "openmotion": { "command": "/absolute/path/to/node", "args": ["--experimental-strip-types", "/absolute/path/to/opengame/mcp.ts"], "env": { "MOTION_DATA_DIR": "/absolute/path/to/opengame-data" } } } } ``` > Keep `MOTION_DATA_DIR` outside the git checkout so your games, generated assets, and provider keys stay cleanly separated from repository updates. See the [full setup guide](docs/opengame-setup.md) and [architecture reference](docs/opengame-architecture.md). ### 12 Dedicated Game MCP Tools OpenGame exposes a complete game-engineering tool surface over local stdio MCP (using the shared `openmotion_game_*` namespace so existing hosts and adapters stay 100% compatible): | MCP Tool | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `openmotion_game_create` | Create a new game draft (2D, 3D with vendored Three.js, or 9:16 `playableAd`) and return the complete agent brief | | `openmotion_game_get` | Read a game card, lifecycle status, and full file inventory | | `openmotion_game_read_file` | Read any source or design file inside a game project | | `openmotion_game_write_files` | Batch-write cohesive game source and design files (up to 100 text files / 8 MiB per owned game) | | `openmotion_game_update_meta` | Merge title, description, controls, cover path, and localized metadata (`zh-CN`, etc.) | | `openmotion_game_validate` | Check `index.html`, CDN policy, deterministic logic exports, and run a 50-tick smoke test | | `openmotion_game_simulate` | Run bounded 3-tier deterministic headless simulations (`reference` win / weak / `idle` loss) | | `openmotion_game_playtest` | Launch isolated headless Chrome (1–4 clients) to test real input controls, `390×844` layout, and console cleanliness | | `openmotion_game_capture_cover` | Capture a clean `1280×720` PNG directly from the game canvas into `assets/cover.png` | | `openmotion_game_trailer` | Record real headless gameplay clips and render an editable ~19-second MP4 trailer | | `openmotion_game_set_status` | Transition lifecycle status (`building`, `ready`, `failed`) | | `openmotion_game_publish` | Revalidate and publish the game into the local Game Studio catalog | Plus **`openmotion_media_use`** (discover & inspect configured BYOK multimodal models) and **`openmotion_assets_use`** (generate images/music/voice/video and run `action: "web_publish"` for one-click cloud share links). [Full MCP contract](docs/mcp-phase1-tools.md) ### Game Engineering Skill & 18 Reference Handbooks Every connected agent can read [`skills/openmotion-game/SKILL.md`](skills/openmotion-game/SKILL.md) (or `openmotion://workflow/game/start` via MCP resources) along with 18 specialized engineering handbooks: | Domain | Reference Guides | | --- | --- | | **Game Design & Structure** | [Brief # llm.asm

**Three complete LLM projects written in 100% pure x86-64 NASM assembly.**
Zero C, zero C++, zero Rust, zero libc, zero libm, zero runtime dependencies.

Assembled directly with `nasm` and linked with `ld`. Every math kernel (`expf`, `sincosf`, `RMSNorm`, `RoPE`, `SiLU`, `Softmax`), AVX2+FMA+F16C GEMM/GEMV engine, BPE tokenizer, `clone()`/`futex()` thread pool, bare-metal SMP kernel, analytical backward pass, AdamW optimizer, and live Unicode Braille TUI is hand-written x86-64 assembly (`17,252` lines total across all three projects).

## The Trilogy

| Project | Binary | Size | Deps | Key Numbers |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| **[01-qwen3-inference/](01-qwen3-inference/)** | `build/asm-llm` | **14,712 B** *(14,008 B `FAST_Q8=0`)* | **0** | Static Linux ELF running `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` (Q8_0, built-in BPE tokenizer, GQA + QK-Norm + RoPE + SwiGLU, single-shot & `--chat` multi-turn KV-cache REPL). **`FAST_Q8=1` (default):** **126.8 tok/s** decode at 40T (**20.7 tok/s** at 1T), **+18% to +36% faster than `llama.cpp` CPU (`Q8_0`) across 1..40T**, **`0.99965`** cosine & **64/64** exact greedy tokens vs PyTorch FP32. |
| **[02-baremetal-os/](02-baremetal-os/)** | `build/asm-llm-os.elf` | **24,252 B** *(23,612 B `FAST_Q8=0`)* | **0** | Bootable bare-metal `Qwen3-0.6B` OS with no Linux or Windows. Multiboot 1 -> Long Mode -> AVX2/FMA/F16C -> ACPI/APIC SMP -> VGA + PS/2 + COM1 multi-turn KV-cache chat (`/clear`, `/think`, `/bench`). **74–94 ms** boot, **134.9 tok/s** KVM EPYC (**23.7 tok/s** 1 vCPU, **136.6 tok/s** peak), **55.4 tok/s** live on Proxmox Xeon E5-2670 v3 with **0 GB** disk. |
| **[03-minigpt-train/](03-minigpt-train/)** | `build/asm-gpt-train` | **32,944 B** | **0** | From-scratch FP32 Mini-GPT trainer and sampler. Register-blocked `6x16` AVX2+FMA SGEMM, full analytical backward pass (**`1.0000000000`** cosine across all 21 gradient tensors vs PyTorch CPU), decoupled AdamW, **27,662 train tok/s**, live 80x24 Braille TUI, `val_loss 4.19 -> 1.51` on TinyShakespeare in 4 min. |

---

## Head-to-Head CPU Decode Benchmark: `llm.asm` vs `llama.cpp` (`Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0`)

Measured on the same machine (**AMD EPYC 7642**, 47C online, 256 MiB L3, DDR4, CPU-only `-ngl 0`), same model (`Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0`: `613.66 MiB` `.asmbin` v2 FP16-scale vs `604.15 MiB` GGUF `Q8_0`), `34` prompt tokens / `64` generated tokens, `3`-run average:

| Threads | `llm.asm` (`FAST_Q8=0`, FP32 act) | `llama.cpp` (`Q8_0`, `-ngl 0`) | **`llm.asm` (`FAST_Q8=1`, 14.7 KB)** | **vs `llama.cpp`** | **Bare-Metal OS KVM (`FAST_Q8=1`)** |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **1** | 7.18 tok/s | 16.63 tok/s | **20.70 tok/s** | **1.24x (+24.5%)** | **23.67 tok/s** |
| **4** | 28.12 tok/s | 51.08 tok/s | **69.24 tok/s** | **1.36x (+35.6%)** | **78.89 tok/s** |
| **8** | 53.09 tok/s | 80.79 tok/s | **103.64 tok/s** | **1.28x (+28.3%)** | **118.08 tok/s** |
| **16** | 77.50 tok/s | 103.03 tok/s | **121.86 tok/s** | **1.18x (+18.3%)** | **134.94 tok/s** |
| **24** | 91.88 tok/s | 104.11 tok/s | **123.72 tok/s** | **1.19x (+18.8%)** | **132.90 tok/s** |
| **32** | 96.63 tok/s | 103.82 tok/s | **122.51 tok/s** | **1.18x (+18.0%)** | **133.75 tok/s** |
| **40** | 98.50 tok/s | 105.08 tok/s | **125.86 tok/s** *(peak 126.81)* | **1.20x (+19.8%)** | — |

*(Note: `llama.cpp` uses batched GEMM for prompt prefill `pp34`, whereas `llm.asm` runs token-by-token GEMV. For autoregressive decode `tg64`, `llm.asm` (`FAST_Q8=1`) combines INT8xINT8 AVX2 `vpmaddubsw`/`vpmaddwd`, `.asmbin` v2 FP16 block scales (`F16C vcvtph2ps`), monotonic next-row prefetch, contiguous head-major KV-cache, and parallel GQA attention — beating `llama.cpp` by +18%..+36% across 1..40 threads while producing bit-exact deterministic outputs across all thread counts. The bare-metal OS gains another ~10% from 2 MiB huge-page identity mapping.)*

## Quick Start

Clone the repo and build everything with `make all`:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/alesha-pro/llm.asm.git
cd llm.asm
make all
```

### 1. Run Qwen3-0.6B Inference in 14 KB (`01-qwen3-inference/`)

```bash
# Export compact .asmbin v2 (FP16 block scales, 613.66 MiB; or --scale-dtype fp32 for legacy v1)
python3 scripts/export_weights.py --model-dir models/qwen3-0.6b-bf16 --out models/qwen3-0.6b-q8_0.asmbin --scale-dtype fp16
# Build with FAST_Q8=1 (default: INT8xINT8 AVX2 + parallel GQA) or FAST_Q8=0 (exact FP32 activations)
make inference FAST_Q8=1
./build/asm-llm -m models/qwen3-0.6b-q8_0.asmbin -p "Explain how a CPU cache works in 3 concise sentences." -n 128 -t 16
# Or start an interactive multi-turn chat preserving the KV-cache across turns:
./build/asm-llm -m models/qwen3-0.6b-q8_0.asmbin --chat -t 16
```

Full step-by-step setup, model download, CLI flags, and benchmarks: **[01-qwen3-inference/README.md](01-qwen3-inference/README.md)**.

### 2. Boot Bare-Metal Qwen3-0.6B OS in 24 KB (`02-baremetal-os/`)

```bash
make os FAST_Q8=1
make os-run MODEL=models/qwen3-0.6b-q8_0.asmbin SMP=16
# Or build a bootable BIOS+UEFI ISO for QEMU / Proxmox VE:
make os-iso MODEL=models/qwen3-0.6b-q8_0.asmbin
```

Full QEMU KVM, bootable ISO, and 0 GB disk Proxmox VE deployment guide: **[02-baremetal-os/README.md](02-baremetal-os/README.md)**.

### 3. Train Mini-GPT from Scratch in 32 KB (`03-minigpt-train/`)

Zero Python required to train or run inference:

```bash
mkdir -p data checkpoints && curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karpathy/char-rnn/master/data/tinyshakespeare/input.txt -o data/tinyshakespeare.txt
make train
./build/asm-gpt-train --data data/tinyshakespeare.txt --steps 400 --seq 128 -t 16 --save checkpoints/shakespeare.ckpt
```

Full training, live Braille TUI, checkpoint chat loop, and PyTorch gradient check guide: **[03-minigpt-train/README.md](03-minigpt-train/README.md)**.

## System Requirements

- **CPU:** x86-64 with **AVX2 + FMA + F16C** (Intel Haswell / AMD Excavator or newer).
- **Build tools:** `nasm` and GNU `binutils` (`ld`, `objcopy`).
  ```bash
  sudo apt install nasm binutils
  ```
- **Phase 1 & 3 runtime:** Any Linux x86-64 kernel. Zero shared libraries (`readelf -d` reports no dynamic section).
- **Phase 2 runtime (optional):** `qemu-system-x86_64` with KVM, or any x86-64 hypervisor/bare-metal machine (Proxmox VE, VirtualBox, real hardware). Building bootable ISOs uses `grub-mkrescue` (`grub-pc-bin`, `grub-efi-amd64-bin`, `mtools`, `xorriso`).
- **Offline tooling (optional):** `python3` + `numpy` only for one-time `Qwen3-0.6B` `.asmbin` export and reference verification (`torch` + `transformers` only if running PyTorch parity checks).

---

## Architecture & Verification Summary

Every phase is built on the same engineering rules: no runtime libraries, deterministic parallel partitioning, and numerical verification against independent Python/PyTorch references.

- **Shared assembly core (`shared/`):** Phase 2 compiles the exact same `math.asm`, `matmul.asm`, `tokenizer.asm`, and `transformer.asm` with `-DBARE_METAL` (swapping Linux `mmap`/`clone`/`write` for physical Multiboot modules, APIC spin-barriers, and VGA+COM1 drivers). Phase 3 reuses `syscalls.asm` and `math.asm`.
- **Phase 1 verification:** All math/SIMD kernels pass unit tests within `1e-7..1e-6` (`init_rope_freqs` FP64 `< 5e-14`) for both `FAST_Q8=1` and `FAST_Q8=0` across v1 FP32 and v2 FP16 scale formats. `FAST_Q8=1` matches PyTorch FP32 `Qwen3-0.6B` with `cosine = 0.9996517` and **64/64 exact greedy tokens** (`FAST_Q8=0` matches the Python Q8_0 reference with `cosine = 1.000000000`). Bit-exact deterministic from `1T` to `40T`.
- **Phase 2 verification:** **100% token-exact and byte-for-byte identical** to Phase 1 across 5 test prompts (English, Russian UTF-8, arithmetic, `--think` mode), multi-turn KV-cache recall + `/clear`, and across `1..32` KVM vCPUs (`134.9 tok/s` at 16 vCPUs). Verified on both QEMU KVM (AMD EPYC 7642) and a real Proxmox VE VM (Intel Xeon E5-2670 v3, 0 GB disk, BIOS GRUB ISO).
- **Phase 3 verification:** Verified against PyTorch FP32 CPU on all **21 parameter tensors** (`worst max_abs_diff = 3.35e-8`, `min cosine_sim = 1.0000000000`), 10-step AdamW + cosine LR + grad-clip trajectory (`max_loss_diff = 4.77e-7`), and bit-exact determinism across `1T`, `8T`, and `16T`.

See each project's README for full tables, memory layouts, and reproduction steps:

- [02-baremetal-os/README.md](02-baremetal-os/README.md)

There's no speaker in a MacBook trackpad, just a small haptic motor that taps the glass so you feel a click.
NO SPEAKER drives that motor up to 4,000 times a second, fast enough to make sound you can hear, and turns it
into a voice. It talks, sings, raps, and becomes an instrument under your finger.

One command. About a minute and a half. No speakers used.

<!-- demo video: drag an .mp4 here in GitHub's editor -->

## 01 / before you start

```text
[ mute your mac ]        it still talks; that's the point
[ put it on a table ]    on your lap it's much quieter
[ hands off the glass ]  until it asks you to touch it
```

**Space** skips a part. **q** or **Ctrl-C** goes to the end.

## 02 / run it

`[ one line ]`

```sh
curl -fsSL a90.com/nospeaker | sh
```

Downloads the latest release to `~/.local/bin/nospeaker` and starts the show. `a90.com/nospeaker` points
to [play.sh](play.sh) in this repo, so you can read what it runs first.

`[ download ]`

Grab `nospeaker.zip` from the [latest release](https://github.com/os6/nospeaker/releases/latest),
unzip it and run `./nospeaker` in Terminal. Signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple.

`[ from source ]`

Needs Xcode or the Command Line Tools (`xcode-select --install`). Builds one program for Apple Silicon
and Intel Macs.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/os6/nospeaker
cd nospeaker
./build.sh
./nospeaker
```

## 03 / play with it

```text
./nospeaker "hello there"            say anything
./nospeaker --voice Daniel "hello"   in another macOS voice
./nospeaker --sweep                  a rising tone, 100 Hz to 4 kHz

--dark                               white on black
--plain                              no visuals, plain text
```

## 04 / needs

A Force Touch trackpad (built into MacBooks from 2015 on, or a Magic Trackpad 2 or newer), and macOS 12 or
later on Apple Silicon, or macOS 13 or later on Intel. Without a Force Touch trackpad, it says so and exits.

```text
tested on

MacBook Pro (Mac17,10)   M5 Max   macOS 27.2.1   everything works
```

Not tested yet: Intel Macs, a Magic Trackpad, and older versions of macOS. MultitouchSupport is private, so
older systems may lack the functions it uses, and loudness differs between trackpads. If you try it on another
Mac, open an issue with your model, your macOS version and how it sounded.

## 05 / how it works

```text
say ──▶ formants ──▶ two tones ──▶ motor ──▶ glass
        per 10 ms    F1 + F2       haptics   sound
```

**Why you can hear it.** The trackpad has no speaker, but the motor moves the glass. Driven back and forth
hundreds or thousands of times a second, the glass vibrates fast enough to make sound you can hear. It's quiet
because the motor is built for short taps, not for sound.

**The motor.** `MultitouchSupport` is the private framework macOS uses for the trackpad. Its function
`MTActuationCreateFromDictionary` takes a description of a vibration, a list of sine tones with a frequency,
a strength and a length each, and `MTActuationActuate` plays it on the motor. Apple's public haptics API only
offers three fixed taps.

**The range.** Measured with the MacBook's own microphone, every semitone from 98 Hz to 3,951 Hz: how loud it
is over a quiet room, and how much of the sound is the note itself.

```text
│                                      ###
│                          #+#     +++#####        #
│                         +#+#+   .+++#####       .#
│              .       ++++#+#+   .+++#####    # #.# #
│   ++        +. . #..+++++#+#++++.+++#####+ #####.###          .#
│   +++#.     +...+#..+++++#+#++++.+++#####+ #####.####+        .#
│  ++++#...   +...+#..+++++#+#++++.+++#####+.#####.####+        .#
│ .++++#...++++...+#..+++++#+#++++.+++#####+.#####.####+  +#    .#
│..++++#...++++...+#..+++++#+#++++.+++#####+.#####.####+#.+#  .#.#
│..++++#...++++...+#..+++++#+#++++.+++#####+.#####.####+#.+#+..#.#
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      131         262         523         1047        2093    3951
   public notes stop at 600 Hz ─┘

across: every semitone, in Hz · up: loudness, +16 to +34 dB
# clean note   + fair   . mostly buzz
```

It's loud from about 100 Hz to 4 kHz, with a few dead spots where the glass resonates. Its loudest, cleanest
notes are around 1 kHz, which covers the most important part of a voice.

**The voice.** macOS's own voice speaks the line into memory. Every 10 ms, linear prediction finds the voice's
two strongest resonances (formants), its loudness and its pitch. The motor plays those two resonances as tones,
restarted on every beat of the pitch, so they buzz like a voice instead of whistling. Hiss sounds (s, f, t)
become quick bursts of high tones. Two resonances beat three: in a blind test they were clearer, and louder,
because the motor's strength is split fewer ways.

It sounds robotic, and it's much easier to follow when you can read along, which is why the show types every
line as it speaks.

**The code.** One Swift file, [nospeaker.swift](nospeaker.swift), with no dependencies.

## 06 / caveats

- **Is it safe?** It never drives the motor past its normal maximum strength. Going past it is possible and
  louder, but the driver starts to stall, so nospeaker doesn't.
- MultitouchSupport is private and undocumented, so a macOS update could break this.

The MultitouchSupport function names were learned from the open-source Tactile project. Everything else was
measured on a MacBook.


items.readme: # Xbox Emulator **Running the Xbox Series X|S library on PC. A continuation of [drycheetah84/TomBox](https://github.com/drycheetah84/TomBox).** The runtime reimplements the console's platform layer (Xbox-flavoured Direct3D 12, precompiled RDNA2 shaders, unified-memory textures, system libraries) so dumped, already-decrypted Xbox Series X|S builds run as normal Windows processes. It is not tied to any single title. This repo tracks our continuation — new titles brought up, platform calls extended, shader stages unlocked. Uses legally obtained, already-decrypted dumps. The runtime does no key extraction or package decryption. **Source code:** the emulator's Rust workspace is in this repo: [`crates/`](crates/), [`tools/`](tools/) and `Cargo.toml`. It contains no game files, binaries or build output. **Contributing:** pull requests are welcome, especially console library functions still marked missing in the [library map](docs/LIBRARY_MAP.md). See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Licensed MIT OR Apache-2.0. ## Status [![system functions](docs/img/badge-imports.svg)](docs/img/progress.svg) [![Direct3D 12.x methods](docs/img/badge-d3d12x.svg)](docs/img/progress.svg) [![RDNA2 instructions](docs/img/badge-instructions.svg)](docs/img/progress.svg) [![shaders translated](docs/img/badge-shaders.svg)](#tested-titles) [![shader stages](docs/img/badge-stages.svg)](docs/img/progress.svg) [![milestones](docs/img/badge-milestones.svg)](#milestones) [![titles examined](docs/img/badge-titles.svg)](#tested-titles) [![Xbox console libraries](docs/img/badge-console.svg)](docs/LIBRARY_MAP.md) [![progress map](docs/img/progress.svg)](docs/img/progress.svg) One square per item. The first four sections use upstream's definitions so the numbers stay comparable: green = done, amber = partial (a stub, a forwarder, or not verified to work), grey = not done — imported system functions of the Fortnite EXE, Direct3D 12.x interface methods, RDNA2 shader instructions the decoder knows, and the eight shader stages (mesh and amplification still grey). The fifth section is ours and covers Xbox console libraries only: the exports of the console OS DLLs (EmbeddedXvd of every analysed title, union, so the newest console OS sets the surface) that no same-named DLL in a PC's C:\Windows\System32 exports, so console-only DLLs (d3d12_xs, xg_xs, xmem, AcpHal, chad, xapu, xcrdapi, the *legacy variants, ...) count in full and modified PC DLLs (kernel32, advapi32, mfplat, ...) only for their console-only exports, plus the GDK wrappers the emulator redirects; plain Windows DLLs (ntdll, msvcrt, ucrtbase, combase, ...) are not shown. Coloured implemented / forwarded / stub / missing; lighter squares are functions an analysed title imports. Per-title import coverage likewise counts only imports from console libraries. Generated by tools/progress/gen.py; per-function tables in docs/LIBRARY_MAP.md, headline numbers in tools/progress/summary.json. ## Milestones Counted live by `tools/progress/gen.py`; full table with evidence in [docs/MILESTONES.md](docs/MILESTONES.md). | Milestone | State | |---|---| | All imported system functions covered (671/671) | done | | Full title shader sweep translated (105,506/105,506) | done | | All Direct3D 12.x methods covered | in progress (map) | | All RDNA2 instructions verified | in progress (map) | | All shader stages (Mesh, Amplification) | in progress (map) | | All Xbox console libraries covered | in progress (map) | | Fortnite boots, first frames, login, hotfix, mode select, BR lobby | done (7 run milestones) | | 3D scene correct | not reached | | Keyboard / controller input | not reached | | Audio | not reached | | Gameplay | not reached | | A second title running | not reached | ## Tested titles | Title | Build | Result | |---|---|---| | Fortnite (Chapter 2 Season 4) | 2.0.1461.7919 | Boots, logs in to a private server, reaches the lobby. 2D interface correct. 3D scene lit but the character material is wrong and bloom shows artifacts. No audio. Not playable. On this machine (2026-11-21): boots, first frames, window on the primary monitor, login complete, hotfix success, game-mode select, Battle Royale lobby (`UI.State.Athena.Frontend`). | | XDefiant | dump examined | **Not run.** Imports and console OS (10.0.22000) mapped in [docs/LIBRARY_MAP.md](docs/LIBRARY_MAP.md); new modules include XCurl, Bink2Scarlett, chad (XDsp*), xapu (XApu*). | | Grand Theft Auto VI | 1.0.2.1 | **Not run** (dump has no executable). Shader package examined: 26,503 shaders, plain compressed Xbox shader containers. Of a 4,000-shader sample all disassemble cleanly; ~⅓ of vertex shaders translate. Blockers: mesh shaders, shaders without root signatures. | ## Our local state - [docs/DEVELOPMENT_LOG.md](docs/DEVELOPMENT_LOG.md) — chronological log - [docs/BLOCKERS.md](docs/BLOCKERS.md) — standing walls - [docs/LIBRARY_MAP.md](docs/LIBRARY_MAP.md) — per-library, per-function status (generated) - [docs/LIBRARY_DISCOVERY.md](docs/LIBRARY_DISCOVERY.md) — what the dumps contain ## Credit Upstream: [drycheetah84/TomBox](https://github.com/drycheetah84/TomBox) (base commit `7e8064f`). The map and badges here are generated in this repo by `tools/progress/gen.py`, which keeps upstream's metric definitions and style for the first four sections.
